title: Darkshore
body: Darkshore is a long, cold strip of misty coast on the northwestern edge of Kalimdor, grey beaches and dark pines pressed against the mountains. Ten thousand years ago it was a rich land of the kaldorei, where Queen Azshara's Highborne kept the twin towns of Ameth'Aran and Bashal'Aran and the city of Mathystra shone in the north. The Sundering left them in ruins. Today the night elves hold only Auberdine, and the land around it is sickening: the Cliffspring River turns foul, the thistle bears go rabid and the Blackwood furbolgs have turned on their old friends.

parts.body: The river's waters show where the sickness comes from. Its source is not these hills at all but Felwood, the corrupted forest beyond the mountains to the east.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Darkshore_(Classic) (long coast, cold and foggy, mountains east, former kaldorei wealth, Ameth'Aran and Bashal'Aran, Sundering, Auberdine only town, taint from Felwood)

parts.body: For a time the war with the Qiraji reaches even this cold coast: great resonating crystals break through the earth, guarded by eroded anubisath.

title: Auberdine
body: Auberdine is the only night elf town on the Darkshore coast, a port of low timber halls among the pines. Elder Thundris Windweaver sees to its affairs with a village council, Sentinels see to its defense, and dwarf smiths have come for the trade. Ships sail from its piers to Rut'theran Village and Azuremyst Isle. Lately great sea creatures have been beaching themselves on the shore in growing numbers, and the town takes it for an ill omen.

parts.body: Through an old friend among the Sentinels, the draenei of Blood Watch have written to Thundris proposing an alliance. He knows their isles were long ago home to his own people, and promises Auberdine's aid.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Auberdine (pre-Cataclysm: only stronghold, low arched wooden buildings among pines, lamp-lit streets, lighthouse, dwarven smithy, village council, Sentinels)

parts.body: The Temple of the Moon's envoy has found a troubling idea in the bones of the beached creatures: they may be fleeing the waters around Teldrassil.

parts.body: From the southern pier the Bravery now crosses the sea to Stormwind Harbor, the town's road to the human kingdom.

title: Bashal'Aran
body: Bashal'Aran was one of the twin towns Queen Azshara gave her Highborne, ruled with Ameth'Aran by her governor Athrikus Narassin and home of his second, the mage Asterion. It fell with the Well of Eternity. Now sprites, grells and satyrs crowd its stones, feeding on the magic that lingers there, yet they shun one shrine on the western bluff, where a blue aura hangs between the pillars and a Highborne specter waits.

parts.body: The specter is Asterion himself, held at the shrine by a seal for more than a thousand years, with only grells and satyrs for company.
sources: page_text 364, 365 (The Lay of Ameth'Aran: twin towns, Athrikus governor, Asterion his second living in Bashal'Aran)

parts.body: With the seal destroyed in the ancient flame of Ameth'Aran, Asterion is free, and he names his jailor: his own former master, Athrikus, who he senses still lives.

title: Ameth'Aran
body: Ameth'Aran, twin of Bashal'Aran, was a town where Azshara's Highborne practiced their magic freely. When the Well of Eternity was destroyed it fell to ruin, and its people did not rest: cursed and wailing Highborne spirits still drift among the broken walls, wielding the implements they used in life. Two great tablets tell the town's story, and an ancient blue flame still burns among the stones.

parts.body: The tablets give the Circle a rare record of the War of the Ancients: brother fighting brother, and Athrikus Narassin coming among his terrified people with a spell that promised them life eternal while all around them perished.
sources: quest 953 description (servants of Azshara practiced their magics, restless Highborne spirits, two tablets)

parts.body: Among the dead wanders Anaya Dawnrunner, whose beloved Cerellean Whiteclaw followed Malfurion into the long sleep in his grief and woke, ages later, to find her spirit here.

title: Tower of Althalaxx
body: The Tower of Althalaxx rises northeast of Auberdine, apart from the twin towns it once watched over: Athrikus Narassin, Azshara's governor, spent his days here rather than among his people. Ten thousand years later it is occupied again, by warlocks of the Cult of the Dark Strand, and the strongest of them keep to the upper room. From the woods nearby, Balthule Shadowstrike watches them for his master in Ashenvale.

parts.body: The master of the upper room is Athrikus Narassin himself, alive after ten thousand years and at the head of the cult.

title: Ruins of Mathystra
body: At the northern end of Darkshore lie the Ruins of Mathystra, once a great bastion of the night elves. The city was shattered when the Well of Eternity was destroyed, and its survivors scattered to smaller villages down the coast. Shards of its magic still linger in relics among the grass and broken stones, and the Stormscale naga hold the ruins now, guarding them fiercely.

parts.body: Onu fears the Twilight's Hammer means to turn this old elven magic to its own ends, and wants Mathystra's relics studied before the cult can use them.

title: Grove of the Ancients
body: Against the mountains due south of Auberdine, the Grove of the Ancients stands among the ruins of an old night elf temple. Here dwells Onu, an Ancient of Lore, patient and sparing with his words, and the night elves count the Ancients as venerable allies and heed their warnings. He finds it strange that naga have come to Darkshore, and stranger still the Twilight's Hammer.

parts.body: When word from Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm at last reaches him, Onu remarks mildly that Fandral always seems in such a hurry. The forest knows all comes in its appointed time, he says, and Shan'do Stormrage understood that.

title: The Master's Glaive
body: In the south of Darkshore a vast blade stands driven into the earth. Onu holds that the Master's Glaive marks where one of the old lords of the earth, defeated long ago, fell. Now the Twilight's Hammer, a cult that worships such masters, camps around it, crying glory and blood for the Old Gods, and its thugs share the cave behind Cliffspring Falls with naga.

parts.body: The old lord is long dead, Onu says, but slivers of its power may still remain, and the cult must be seeking them.
sources: quest 944 description and reward text (old lord impaled by the glaive, slivers of power, cult worships old lords of the earth)

parts.body: Their tome maddens the eye, and its one torn page comes from an ancient text written by elves: the cult is using old elven magic to bring its masters back.
